1#main: To conduct oneself with honor toward a Sefer Torah, and the law of its accessories. In it are 19 seifim. A person is obligated to conduct himself with great honor toward a Sefer Torah; and it is a mitzvah to designate a place for it and honor that place and adorn it greatly. And he should not spit opposite a Sefer Torah; nor expose his nakedness opposite it; nor stretch out his legs opposite it; nor place it on his head like a burden; nor turn his back to it unless it is ten tefachim higher than him. Rather he sits before it with gravity, awe, and fear—for it is the faithful witness over all who come into the world, as it says, "And it shall be there with you for a witness"—and one honors it according to one's ability.
2#main: One who sees a Sefer Torah when it is being carried is obligated to stand before it; and everyone stands until the one carrying it stands still and brings it to its place, or until it is covered from their eyes. {Rama: But before our chumashim one need not stand (Beit Yosef in the name of the Rambam); and some are stringent (Rashba siman 144). One who hears the sound of one carrying a Sefer Torah—even if he does not see it—is obligated to stand (Beit Yosef in the name of Rav Rabbenu Menachem).}
3#main: If he was going from place to place with a Sefer Torah with him, he should not place it in a sack and put it on the donkey and ride on it; rather he places it in his lap opposite his heart and rides on the donkey. And if he feared thieves, it is permitted.
4#main: One should not hold a Sefer Torah and enter with it into a privy or bathhouse or cemetery, even if it is wrapped in a cloth and placed in its case; nor read in it until he distances four amot from the dead or from the cemetery, or from the privy; nor hold a Sefer Torah without a cloth.
5#main: One does not throw sacred writings—even halachot and aggadot. (And it is forbidden to turn them face down; and when one finds them thus, one must turn them over) (Maharil).
6#main: Amulets—if they are covered in hide, it is permitted to enter with them into a privy; and if not, it is forbidden.
7#main: It is forbidden to sit on a bed on which a Sefer Torah lies. {Rama: And all the more so it is forbidden to place it on the ground; and the same law applies to other books (Beit Yosef in the name of R' Rabbenu Menachem and in the name of Orach Chaim and Kol Bo). And even on the steps made before the Holy Ark it is forbidden to place books (Hagahos Maimoniyos). And a person should not place a Sefer Torah on his knees with both forearms upon it (Maharil). And it appears to me that the same law applies to other books.}
8#main: A house in which there is a Sefer Torah—one should not use it for his bed until he removes it; and if he has no place to remove it, he makes before it a partition ten tefachim high. But by placing a vessel within a vessel that is not designated, it is not permitted except for tefillin and other sacred writings and chumashim—but not for a Sefer Torah. And the Rambam permits even for a Sefer Torah. And if he spread his tallit over the chest in which it is placed, it is considered like a vessel within a vessel.
9#main: All impure persons—even niddot—are permitted to hold a Sefer Torah and read from it, provided their hands are not soiled or dirty.
10#main: A Sefer Torah that wore out or became invalid—one places it in an earthenware vessel and buries it next to a Torah scholar; and this is its genizah.
11#main: Cloths of books that wore out—one makes them shrouds for a met mitzvah; and this is their genizah.
12#main: A case prepared for a Sefer Torah in which it was placed; and likewise the cloths, the ark, and the tower in which they place a Sefer Torah—even though they do not place a Sefer Torah in it when it is alone, but only when it is in its case; and likewise a chair prepared to place a Sefer Torah upon it and upon which it was placed—all are accessories of sanctity and are forbidden. And after they wear out or break, they are put in genizah.
13#main: An ark that broke—it is permitted to make another small one from it; but it is forbidden to make from it a chair for a Sefer Torah. And a chair that broke—it is permitted to make from it a small chair, and forbidden to make from it a small stool (meaning: a small bench) for a chair.
14#main: The bimot on which the one who holds the book stands do not have the sanctity of a Sefer Torah; but they have sanctity by reason of the synagogue.
15#main: Everything one makes for a Sefer Torah—if he made it on condition to use its remainder for another accessory, if he wishes the condition is effective.
16#main: Silver and gold ornaments made for a Sefer Torah for decoration are accessories of sanctity, and it is forbidden to use them for mundane purposes unless to buy with them a Sefer Torah or chumash.
17#main: Everything forbidden to change to a lighter sanctity—if the seven good men of the city sold it in the presence of the people of the city, it is permitted.
18#main: An individual who sells his Sefer Torah and its accessories—some permit using its money; and some forbid. (And if it had errors, all permit it (Rivash siman 286); and see in Orach Chaim siman 153.)
19#main: It is permitted to place a Sefer Torah on a Sefer Torah; and one places chumashim on Prophets and Writings; but one does not place Prophets and Writings on chumashim, nor chumashim on a Sefer Torah. {Rama: But Writings on Prophets (or the reverse) is permitted (Beit Yosef in the name of Ran in the name of Tosafot, first chapter of Bava Batra). And all this speaks of two bindings, each bound by itself; but in one binding, all is permitted (Mordechai, chapter HaShutfin). And see above siman 246 that it is forbidden to contemplate words of Torah in filthy places—and this is because of honor of Torah.}
